Title: Document 1
Content: . . .The British came and went, and when they went the center could not hold, and things fell apart. In truth there was no real center, the region has always been divided by ancient disparities [differences] of the languages of the Punjab and Gujarat, mountains and the deserts, and Islam and Hinduism. By `1947`, the forces of postcolonial nationalism and religious separatism broke the subcontinent into `text(two)`, and later `text(three)`, major pieces; India, Pakistan and Bangladesh. The British, exhausted by `text(two)` world wars, and aware that the `text(days)` of the empire were coming to a close, did not cover themselves in glory in the manner of their leaving.

On `text(June 3, 1947)`, the announcement was made in the House of Commons: The British would withdraw — India was to be partitioned into the `text(two)` independent dominions of India and Pakistan. `text(Seventy-three days)` later, on `text(August 15)`, they were all but gone. . . .
